Cluster C Personality Disorders

avoidant · dependent · obsessive-compulsive personality disorderWhich fear drives the pattern?

Practice
  1. 29-year-old man brought by his sister, worried he is lonely has wanted a partner for years but declines every invitation sure coworkers find him dull; turned down a promotion to lead meetings no odd beliefs; affect anxious, not flat → Avoidant personality disorder → wants closeness but avoids people, work roles and new contacts for fear of criticism, as a pervasive pattern: avoidant personality disorder; schizoid patients want no closeness, and social anxiety disorder is often tied to specific situations
  2. 24-year-old man brought by his father, who worries he has no friends spends evenings alone with model trains; never dated, wants no partner shrugs when his manager praises his work normal early development; flat affect; no odd beliefs → Schizoid personality disorder → no wish for closeness, solitary pastimes, flat affect and indifference to praise: schizoid personality disorder; avoidant patients want closeness but fear rejection, and autism needs early childhood social deficits with repetitive behaviors
  3. 34-year-old woman at a routine visit; works alone overnight in a warehouse would like a partner but will not date unless sure she will be liked speaks softly; avoids eye contact no odd beliefs; no psychotic symptoms → Avoids new activities for fear of embarrassment → wants a partner but avoids people for fear of rejection, so avoidant personality disorder is suspected; confirm with a second avoidant criterion, avoiding new activities that may embarrass; the other choices are dependent and schizoid criteria
  4. 38-year-old woman brought by her sister after her husband left within 2 weeks moved in with a new partner who pays her bills has always asked her sister what to wear; hates being alone mood not depressed; no self-harm → Dependent personality disorder → a lifelong need for others to decide and care for her, helplessness alone and a rush into a new caretaking relationship: dependent personality disorder; borderline patients swing between submission and rage, and avoidant patients withdraw until sure of acceptance
  5. 45-year-old engineer referred after missing a third project deadline redoes drawings until every detail is perfect; will not let others help says his standards are simply correct; no intrusive thoughts or rituals works most weekends; few friends → Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder → perfectionism that blocks finishing, refusal to delegate and devotion to work, seen by the patient as right: OCPD; OCD has unwanted obsessions relieved by rituals, and schizoid detachment comes from no wish for closeness, not devotion to work
  6. 27-year-old woman with avoidant personality disorder asks for help wants friends but declines every invitation, sure she will be criticized no self-harm, mood swings or impulsivity no odd beliefs or perceptual disturbances; not depressed → Cognitive behavioral therapy → avoidant personality disorder: psychotherapy, where CBT may help reframe beliefs about self-worth and ease avoidance; dialectical behavior therapy is for borderline personality disorder, and a low-dose antipsychotic may help as an adjunct for severe paranoia in schizotypal personality disorder
Pairs with Cluster B Personality Disorders covers the dramatic, emotional or erratic disorders. Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders covers OCD and its treatment. Panic Disorder and Other Anxiety covers social anxiety disorder. Hears Voices or Holds Odd Beliefs covers schizotypal and paranoid personality disorder. Trauma, Stress and Dissociative Disorders covers adjustment disorder.
Transferable rule

In a lifelong anxious pattern, ask what the patient fears: rejection (avoidant), being left to fend for oneself (dependent), or losing order and control (obsessive-compulsive); a patient who simply wants to be alone is schizoid, cluster A.
